jobs.description:
GC Corporation was founded in Japan in 1921 and has grown to become one of the leading companies in the development, manufacture, and distribution of a very wide range of dental products. Since 1972, our European headquarters, GC Europe NV, has been located in Leuven, Belgium. The GC Group includes several subsidiaries within Europe, whose development, manufacturing, and distribution of products for specific areas of dentistry and dental technology round out our product portfolio. Our warehouses distribute our products throughout Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

Tasks

- Build and maintain strong relationships with orthodontists, dental professionals, and key customers.

- Introduce new products, communicate innovations, and support sales campaigns to customers.

- Identify new business opportunities through proactive prospecting, referrals, networking, trade shows, and industry events.

- Act as the primary point of contact for customers, ensuring timely follow-up and excellent customer service.

- Understand customer needs through consultative conversations and recommend suitable orthodontic solutions based on individual requirements.

- Conduct product presentations, demonstrations, and sales meetings using professional sales materials and clinical knowledge.

- Drive sales growth by presenting customer-focused solutions and demonstrating the value of the GC Orthodontics portfolio.

- Maintain accurate customer records, sales activities, and follow-up actions in the CRM system.

- Develop and execute territory plans to maximize customer retention and business growth.

- Collaborate closely with internal teams, including Marketing, Customer Service, and Product Management, to ensure excellent customer experience.

- Continuously develop product knowledge, sales skills, and industry expertise through training, coaching, and professional development activities.

Requirements

- Fluent in Dutch and English; German language skills are considered an advantage

As a maintenance technician, you will work in a large, fully automated distribution centre where technology is constantly in motion. Conveyor systems, roller conveyors, lifts and other automated installations ensure that enormous volumes of goods are moved throughout the warehouse. If a system comes to a standstill, that is where your work becomes interesting: identifying the cause of the problem and getting the system back up and running as quickly as possible.

You will work with a broad combination of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and control technology. One fault may be caused by a mechanical component, while the next may require electrical troubleshooting or analysing the control system. You will look beyond simply replacing a faulty component: you will determine the root cause and identify what is needed to resolve the issue properly.

Using advanced monitoring applications, you can see what is happening within the system and systematically identify technical and system-related faults. You will carry out repairs and maintenance and accurately document significant breakdowns and maintenance activities.

It is precisely this combination that makes the role so interesting: rather than working on a single machine, you will work with an entire automated system in which different technologies come together. You will have the freedom to investigate faults independently, develop solutions and further expand your knowledge of control technology and PLC systems.

- You have experience as a technician in electrical engineering, mechatronics, control technology and/or the maintenance of machinery and installations
- You have experience analysing and resolving technical faults
- You are able to work independently, think in terms of solutions and remain calm when an installation comes to a standstill
- You have an interest in control technology; experience with PLCs is an advantage
